name: # The LIVE cross-port divergence ledger -- the AUTHORITATIVE list.
# DIVERGENCE.md at the repository root explains the shape of these
# disagreements and points here; this file is what actually RUNS, so if
# the two ever disagree, this one wins.
# Six tab-separated columns. `go` and `ts` are what each port ACTUALLY
# produces today, as JSON, or ERROR:<code>. `opts` is a JSON object of
# make() options, or `-` for a stock parser.
# Every row is asserted by BOTH runners: the Go runner must reproduce the
# `go` column and the TS runner the `ts` column, on every run. So a
# divergence that gets FIXED fails this suite as loudly as one that
# regresses, and the row must then be deleted. That is the whole point —
# go/doc/differences.md is prose, and prose rots: through this session it
# claimed 2.e3 and 1e999 still diverged for some time after they were
# aligned, and claimed base-prefixed overflow was aligned before it was.
# A ledger nothing executes is documentation, not a gate.
# Adding a row here is an admission of parity debt, not a way to silence a
# failure. Fix the divergence if you can; record it here only when you
# cannot, with a justification a reader can act on.
string-replace-control
justification: TS string.replace can map a control character to a replacement, making it legal string body. The Go string matcher rejects the raw control character before replacement is consulted, reporting unprintable. (go/doc/differences.md said unterminated_string; this ledger caught that on its first run — the prose predated the error-code alignment.) Replacement of PRINTABLE characters is aligned (see the control row below), and the unprintable error scan does honour replace mappings when locating the first offending character — only this legality question differs.

name: string-replace-printable
justification: Control row, not a divergence: printable replacement is aligned. Kept adjacent so a fix to the row above cannot be mistaken for a regression here.
